panel_intro: One question at a time — nothing here is submitted anywhere.

pedal.text: Does the brake pedal feel soft, go to the floor, or fail to slow the vehicle?

options.label: Yes, the pedal itself feels wrong

noise.text: Do you hear grinding, or a metal-on-metal sound when braking?

pedal_failure.title: Do Not Drive — Call a Tow
pedal_failure.summary: A pedal that feels soft, sinks to the floor, or doesn't slow the car is a safety-critical failure. This is never worth risking a drive, even a short one.
pedal_failure.confidence_text: Pedal-feel problems are one of the clearest do-not-drive signs there is.
not_to_do: Don't test the brakes further by driving to "see how bad it is."
Don't rely on the parking brake as a substitute for working brakes.
Don't assume it's minor just because the car still moves and stops eventually.
before_help_checklist: Keep the vehicle stopped and stable if possible.
Use hazard lights and warning triangles if available.
Note exactly what felt wrong — soft, sinking, or no response.
Avoid restarting or moving the vehicle further.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with the tow company.
lines: Hi, my brake pedal feels unsafe — soft, sinking, or not slowing the car. It's at [location description].
Can you confirm total price, ETA, and where it will be taken?

pedal_failure.next_action: Have a mechanic inspect the brake lines and master cylinder before driving it again.

grinding.title: Do Not Drive — Call a Tow
grinding.summary: Grinding or metal-on-metal sound usually means the brake pads are worn through and metal is contacting the rotor. Continuing to drive risks losing braking entirely and damaging the rotors further.
grinding.confidence_text: Grinding is a clear, well-understood warning sign, not something to wait out.
not_to_do: Don't keep driving "just a little further" once you hear grinding.
Don't ignore it because the brakes still technically work for now.
Don't assume it's a quick, cheap fix without having it inspected.
before_help_checklist: Note when the grinding started and whether it's constant or only sometimes.
Avoid hard braking if you must move the vehicle at all.
Keep the vehicle stopped and stable if possible.
Use hazard lights if you're not in a safe parking spot.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with the tow company.
lines: Hi, my brakes are grinding — metal on metal. The vehicle is at [location description].
Can you confirm total price, ETA, and where it will be taken?

grinding.next_action: Have a mechanic check the pads and rotors — grinding this far along often means both need replacing.

brake_light.title: Do Not Drive — Call a Tow
brake_light.summary: A dedicated brake warning light usually indicates low brake fluid, a hydraulic problem, or the parking brake being engaged. Treat it as safety-critical until it's checked.
brake_light.confidence_text: This light can mean several different things, from a simple parking-brake issue to a real hydraulic problem — a technician needs to check it either way.
not_to_do: Don't assume it's just the parking brake without confirming.
Don't top off brake fluid yourself and keep driving without knowing why it's low.
Don't ignore the light because the pedal still feels normal for now.
before_help_checklist: Confirm the parking brake is fully released.
Note whether the pedal feel has changed at all.
Avoid unnecessary driving until it's checked.
Keep the vehicle stopped and stable if possible.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with the tow company.
lines: Hi, my brake warning light is on and I'd rather not drive it. It's at [location description].
Can you confirm total price, ETA, and where it will be taken?

brake_light.next_action: Have a mechanic check the brake fluid level and hydraulic system before driving it again.

abs_light.title: Safe to Reassess
abs_light.summary: An ABS light alone (with a normal-feeling pedal and no grinding) usually means the anti-lock system has an issue, while regular braking often still works. It's not usually an emergency, but it should be checked soon.
abs_light.confidence_text: ABS issues alone are typically less urgent than a full brake warning light, but this tool can't rule out something more serious — if the pedal feel changes at all, treat it as a tow situation instead.
not_to_do: Don't ignore it indefinitely — ABS helps you keep control while braking hard, especially on wet or icy roads.
Don't assume normal braking is unaffected without paying attention.
Don't drive aggressively in poor conditions until it's checked.
before_help_checklist: Note when the light came on and whether anything changed beforehand.
Pay attention to how the brakes feel during normal, gentle stops.
Avoid hard braking or poor-weather driving until it's checked.
Get it inspected within the next day or two, not indefinitely.

phone_script.intro: Worth calling ahead so the shop is ready for you.
lines: Hi, my ABS light is on but the brakes feel normal otherwise.
Can you take a look at it soon?
Is this something I can drive in to have checked, or should I get a tow?

abs_light.next_action: If the pedal feel changes or you hear any noise at all, stop and treat it as a tow situation instead.
